purpose: Fictional missing railway clerk photograph for case introduction and journal
prompt: Use case: historical-scene. Asset type: in-world photograph for a 1920s Birmingham, Alabama noir detective game's case notebook. Create a single authentic-looking 1929 black-and-white gelatin silver studio portrait of a fictional railway clerk, Samuel Price, about 35, tired eyes, neatly side-parted hair, plain white collared shirt, dark waistcoat and loose tie, ordinary working man rather than movie star. Chest-up portrait, direct gaze, restrained expression, softly mottled dark studio backdrop. Square image containing one slightly worn cream-bordered rectangular photograph, fully visible, no other objects. Subtle film grain, fine scratches, aged paper edges, convincing archival photographic detail, gentle warm silver/cream tones and deep charcoal shadows. No text, writing, typography, badge, branding, watermark, modern clothing, weapons or dramatic props. Keep face clear at notebook thumbnail size.
